name: postquant
description: A post-quantum L1 whose entire state machine is a market in key/value space. Every signature is ML-DSA (FIPS 204, lattice), every commitment is SHA3-256, and there is no elliptic curve anywhere in the trust path — a curve is exactly the thing Shor's algorithm takes apart. There is one thing to own on this chain, a key in the store, and the whole protocol is the market for it: write gas per byte (a key byte costs 4x a value byte, and a value declared as a hash is cheaper still — the chain prices commitments below blobs), witness gas per byte of signature (an ML-DSA-44 signature is 2420 bytes against ed25519's 64, and a chain that charges a flat 21000 is quietly subsidising its own witnesses), and rent per byte-hour against a prepaid escrow. When the escrow runs dry the entry expires and anyone may sweep it for the bond the writer put up, which is what makes expiry real rather than advisory. The fee market is EIP-1559 over state growth instead of execution gas. Keys can be listed and bought with their remaining lease. Consensus is a single proposer — authority, not agreement — but verify replays every block from genesis and re-checks every state root and every signature, which is the check that would still matter under any consensus. REST, the browser console and 22 MCP tools on one port, off the same functions.
backend: python stdlib only (http.server + hashlib) — no dependencies, ML-DSA and ML-KEM implemented in pq/
frontend: console.html — the tip, the store, the market, write/quote, wallets; served at /postquant
state: ~/.mod/postquant — keys.json (32-byte seeds, mode 0600, never committed), <chain_id>/blocks.jsonl (the log, the truth), <chain_id>/state.json (a snapshot, discarded if it disagrees with the log)

crypto.hash: SHA3-256 everywhere: addresses, tx ids, Merkle roots, commitments
crypto.addresses: pq + first 20 bytes of domain-separated SHA3-256 over the ML-DSA public key

economics.write_gas: per byte of key (400), value (100 raw / 40 hash), witness (3), settled at a floating base fee that is burned
economics.rent: 1000 nq per byte-hour against a prepaid escrow; expiry makes the entry sweepable for its bond
economics.fee_market: EIP-1559 over state growth: target 4096 bytes/block, +-12.5% per block

auth.gate: optional — writes only, and only when ~/.mod/postquant/server.secret exists
auth.why: those routes spend PQ or touch the keystore; every route that only reads the chain is open, because a chain nobody can read is not one

endpoints.writes: POST /set /del /fund /sweep /list /buy /transfer /wallet /faucet /mine — JSON bodies, same args as the tools

env.POSTQUANT_PORT: port for API, console and MCP (default 51030)
env.POSTQUANT_HEARTBEAT: seconds between empty blocks so rent keeps settling (default 60)
